title: Route experiments: add customer guide + stickiness key and metrics interpretation
author: Dylan Brooks
description: This PR adds the initial customer-facing documentation for Route experiments (route-level A/B/n testing) in Redwood Console Rollouts. It focuses on: (1) what route experiments are and when to use them, (2) how deterministic assignment works and how to choose/pass a stickiness key to avoid skew, (3) how to interpret the built-in metrics (latency/cost/error/throughput + optional quality signals) and guardrails in Console, and (4) troubleshooting common beta issues (missing attribution on streaming retries, propagation lag/stale results, skew when sticky key is low entropy). The guide is intentionally light on statistical significance claims; it documents basic deltas and guardrail thresholds only (per GA scope). It also documents headers and SDK helpers surfaced during beta so users can self-debug variant assignment. Includes updates to the navigation, terminology glossary, and a small FAQ entry on audit logs and RBAC. Related: ENG-9032 (docs), PM-482 (GA requirements). Support context: SUP-24877 (streaming attribution), SUP-24910 (stale results), SUP-24944 (audit export fields). Checklist: [x] New guide page + screenshots/placeholders [x] Stickiness key guidance + examples (Python/TS) [x] Metrics definitions (p50/p95/p99, cost attribution, error rate) [x] Troubleshooting + known pitfalls [x] Link to runbooks/Console UI concepts without exposing internal-only endpoints [x] Doc site nav + lint/link checks

review_conversation: Marissa Cole (Product): "Thanks for getting this in before beta expansion. Two requests: (1) make it explicit that we do not provide statistical significance in GA; use 'directional deltas' wording. Dylan Brooks (Author): "Updated 'How to read results' to say 'directional deltas' and added a callout that significance testing is not included in GA. Also reworked Guardrails to describe default soft-stop + notification and that some orgs can enable automatic stop with admin controls; removed internal flag names."

Logan Wright (Telemetry): "Metrics section: please don’t imply cost is exact per-request. We should describe cost attribution as aggregated from token usage + pricing model, and mention that results can lag due to aggregation windows. Also: the header names in the examples don’t match what we emit; we use `x-redwood-experiment-id` and `x-redwood-variant-id` (lowercase in docs is fine), plus `x-redwood-sticky-key` is request-side only." Added a 'Results freshness' callout: typical delay 5–15 minutes depending on dataset + region."

Jordan Lee (Policy Engine): "Stickiness key guidance is good, but please add a warning about low-entropy defaults (e.g., missing user id causing many requests to share the same key).
